label: Q4 2026
overview: So far this quarter's news is dominated by rain. Monsoon and autumn storms have triggered slope failures in residual soils, tuff and road cuts across Vietnam, Italy, Chile and Indonesia, and caused urban sinkholes in Mexico, Chile, Ecuador and South Korea, where leaking pipes, poor backfill and drainage lie behind collapses that swallowed cars and, in one Mexican case, led to a negligence finding after a death (S57). Two strands go beyond emergencies: retaining-wall failures and an excavation sinkhole that occurred despite a completed underground safety assessment in South Korea are prompting questions of accountability, and energy-related underground works are under pressure, with further cost rises at Snowy 2.0 and a patent for underground hydrogen storage. Unusually, the most widely syndicated item is a scientific discovery rather than a failure: a giant karst doline in Phong Nha-Ke Bang, reported in at least five language editions. All 60 stories were collected over just three days (22–24 October). Many are translated duplicates of Vietnam.vn items, and the Google News editions are a poor guide to where stories happened, so the balance should be refreshed before the meeting.

story.title: Abergeldie awarded patent for underground hydrogen storage solution

picks.angle: Which ground conditions and geomechanical criteria make a rock mass suitable for storing hydrogen underground, and where does blind boring fit alongside salt caverns and lined rock caverns?
picks.why: Underground hydrogen storage is an emerging market for geotechnical engineers, and the patent gives a concrete industry hook that can be paired with P17 on cyclic loading of storage caverns.

picks.angle: What ground-related risks lie behind the repeated cost increases at Snowy 2.0, now put at A$22.2bn, and what do they mean for risk allocation on pumped hydro caverns?
picks.why: Snowy 2.0 is the flagship pumped hydro project of the energy transition, and its overruns concern every tunnelling and cavern specialist in the readership.

story.title: 标签稀缺条件下基于跨域迁移学习的无人机岩体裂隙网络自动分割方法
story.title_en: Automatic segmentation of rock mass fracture networks from UAV imagery using cross-domain transfer learning under scarce labels.

picks.angle: Can transfer learning reliably map rock-mass fracture networks from UAV imagery when labelled data are scarce, and is it accurate enough to feed slope and support design?
picks.why: It is the only digital story in the window. It addresses a real practice bottleneck, the shortage of labelled data, and links well to P9 and P20.

story.title: Sụt trượt đất nghiêm trọng ở Nam Gia Nghĩa
story.title_en: Serious landslides in South Gia Nghia

picks.angle: How do rainfall infiltration and slope geometry trigger serious failures in weathered residual soils, as at Nam Gia Nghia, and how should such slopes be investigated and stabilised?
picks.why: It is the highest-rated hazards story and stands for a season of residual-soil landslides in Vietnam's Central Highlands that will still be relevant when the issue appears.

story.title: Kè chống sạt lở hơn 57 tỉ đồng ở Thanh Hóa vừa làm xong đã sụt lún, đứt gãy
story.title_en: 57-billion-dong erosion revetment in Thanh Hoa subsides and cracks right after completion

picks.angle: Why did a newly completed 57-billion-dong erosion revetment in Thanh Hoa subside and crack, and which foundation, scour and design checks would have prevented it?
picks.why: A failure immediately after completion raises questions about design and construction quality control that a technical readership can learn from.

story.title: M4 landslip work begins as part of wider repair programme

picks.angle: How is a landslipped motorway embankment on the M4 being diagnosed and repaired, and what drainage and monitoring measures will prevent the slip recurring?
picks.why: It is a planned asset-management repair programme rather than an emergency, so it gives a useful counterpoint to the many rain-triggered failures.

story.title: En perçant 361 trous dans ses fondations en 1934 pour la redresser, les ingénieurs de Mussolini ont littéralement fait pencher la tour de Pise encore plus
story.title_en: Mussolini's engineers drilled 361 holes under Pisa's foundations in 1934 to straighten it, making it lean more.

picks.angle: Why did drilling 361 holes beneath Pisa's foundations in 1934 increase the tilt, and what does it teach about controlled soil removal and differential settlement in stabilisation works?
picks.why: It is an evergreen, widely read hook that connects a historical error with the successful underexcavation techniques modern practice relies on.

story.title: Behavior of Square-Round Shaft Combination Helical Piles and Anchors

picks.angle: How do square-round shaft combination helical piles and anchors carry load, and can their capacity be predicted reliably enough to reduce dependence on site load tests?
picks.why: Helical piles are a growing low-carbon, rapid-install foundation, and the story gives practitioners design-relevant findings.

story.title: 장종태, "굴착 현장 싱크홀...지하안전평가 받고도 땅 꺼졌다"
story.title_en: Sinkhole at excavation site: ground sank even after underground safety assessment

picks.angle: Why did the ground sink at an excavation that had passed an underground safety assessment, and what gaps in such assessments let groundwater and soil loss go undetected?
picks.why: It questions how effective a statutory pre-construction assessment is, which matters to regulators and designers everywhere.

story.title: Más de 300 barrios en riesgo por las lluvias, socavón en la Eloy Alfaro pone en duda la infraestructura subterránea de Quito
story.title_en: More than 300 neighbourhoods at risk from rain; Eloy Alfaro sinkhole casts doubt on Quito's underground infrastructure

picks.angle: What does the Eloy Alfaro sinkhole reveal about ageing buried infrastructure and rain-sensitive ground beneath more than 300 at-risk Quito neighbourhoods?
picks.why: It gives a city-scale view of how water networks and volcanic-valley soils interact, and it represents South America in a theme otherwise led by Asia.

story.title: Metro Bến Thành - Tham Lương cuối năm 2026 làm cả 11 nhà ga
story.title_en: Ben Thanh - Tham Luong metro to have all 11 stations completed by end of 2026

picks.angle: Which deep excavation and tunnelling methods will deliver 11 metro stations in Ho Chi Minh City's soft, water-bearing soils, and what settlement risks must be controlled?
picks.why: Station works are due by the end of 2026, so the story will still be current when the issue appears and can be followed up.

picks.angle: What geotechnical challenges arise in anchoring floating offshore wind in variable seabed soils under extreme and cyclic loading, and where do current design methods fall short?
picks.why: Floating wind is a key offshore growth area, and this is the theme's top-rated story, from a specialist trade source.

story.title: Quảng Trị: Biển xâm thực nghiêm trọng đe dọa đê kè và đời sống người dân
story.title_en: Quang Tri: Severe sea erosion threatens dykes and residents' livelihoods

picks.angle: How do sea erosion and scour undermine sea-dyke foundations on Quang Tri's sandy coast, and which revetment and toe designs suit eroding shorelines?
picks.why: Coastal erosion threatening dykes is a growing climate-adaptation problem, and the piece can draw on P19 for wave-induced pore pressures.

story.title: Hai căn nhà đổ sập do sạt lở bờ sông Tiền
story.title_en: Two houses collapse due to Tien River bank erosion

picks.angle: What riverbank erosion and instability processes caused two houses to collapse on the Tien River, and how can bank stability be assessed near Mekong settlements?
picks.why: Mekong bank collapse is a recurring and serious hazard for settlements on the river.

story.title: Primeval forest grows at bottom of 120-meter-deep sinkhole in central Vietnam

picks.angle: How do karst dissolution and cave-roof collapse produce a 120 m deep doline, and what do such features teach about detecting and characterising cavities in limestone terrain?
picks.why: The doline discovery was reported in many language editions, and the English-language source makes an accessible entry into karst characterisation.

story.title: Minvu avanza en 121 casos de apoyo habitacional en la Villa El Mirador de Arauco y prepara estudio de suelos
story.title_en: Minvu advances 121 housing support cases in Villa El Mirador, Arauco, and prepares soil study

picks.angle: What soil investigation should precede housing support works at Villa El Mirador in Arauco, and how should ground conditions determine foundation choice after a sinkhole?
picks.why: It follows the Arauco sinkhole (S31), where an official said the site was not optimal, and shows site investigation being commissioned after the fact.

story.title: CEDH acredita negligencia del Ayuntamiento de Guasave por muerte de profesor que cayó en socavón
story.title_en: CEDH finds negligence by Guasave municipality in death of teacher who fell into sinkhole

picks.angle: What duty of care do municipalities owe the public over known ground-collapse hazards, and what does the Guasave negligence finding mean for inspection and asset management?
picks.why: The finding by a human rights commission puts sinkhole management squarely in the domain of public accountability, which goes well beyond the engineering.

story.title: Quais são as opções para o Monte Mot em Quy Nhon: nivelá-lo ou preservar o sítio histórico?
story.title_en: What are the options for Mot Mountain in Quy Nhon: level it or preserve the historic site?

picks.angle: What geotechnical assessments are needed to compare levelling Mot Mountain with conserving its historic site, including rock quality, excavation stability and the use of the levelled ground?
picks.why: It is a live public debate where geotechnical evidence should inform a heritage decision.

story.title: Rescatan el cuerpo sin vida del minero que había quedado atrapado en un socavón en Gámeza
story.title_en: Body of miner trapped in a tunnel collapse in Gámeza recovered

picks.angle: What ground and support conditions lead to fatal collapses in small-scale mine tunnels such as Gámeza's, and how can rescue teams allow for continuing instability?
picks.why: It is a reminder that informal and small-scale mining remains a deadly geotechnical problem.

regional.summary: The listing is heavily weighted towards Asia, and above all Vietnam, which accounts for roughly 24 stories. Many of these are translated duplicates syndicated through Vietnam.vn and picked up in other editions. Latin America is well represented through sinkhole and landslide stories from Mexico and Chile, Europe mainly through Italy, while Australasia has only the energy stories and Africa has no stories at all, even though the Egypt and Senegal editions carried items.

covered.comment: Landslides, subsidence, coastal and river erosion, karst dolines, the Ho Chi Minh City metro and the Mot Mountain debate. Duplication is heavy (S16/S20, S7/S21, S42/S47, S35/S59/S60, S19/S51–S54).
An excavation sinkhole, repeated retaining-wall collapses and the start of a geotechnical survey for a bridge. The stories have a strong regulatory angle.
Research-led items only: UAV fracture segmentation and an analytical cavity-response study.
Urban and coastal sinkholes in Mazatlán, Escobedo, Tabasco, Torreón and Coatzacoalcos, plus the Guasave negligence finding. These were collected under the Colombia and Argentina editions.
The Concepción debris flow and the El Bosque and Arauco sinkholes, with a follow-up soil study.

covered.region: Ecuador, Argentina, Colombia and Peru (South America)
covered.comment: One story each: the Quito sinkhole, the Corrientes riverfront subsidence, the Gámeza mine collapse and a sinkhole in Aucapán, which appears to be from Peru's San Martín region.
Four rain-triggered landslides and the historical Pisa story.
The M4 landslip, floating wind, retaining walls in Yalta and Samara, and the A14 tunnel reconstruction.
Snowy 2.0 costs (two duplicate stories) and an underground hydrogen storage patent.
